amendments: A1: the nine spectator audiences are three declarations (Move, Attack, Physical) x three withheld audiences (player-stale, gm-stale, gm-unassigned); the three gm-participant rows are the non-spectating-GM positive controls. All twelve are built on ordinary 1v1 tactical matches with fixture branding; none claims a real mission match or the real mission GM role.

A2 (live stale-first, R1): the stale watcher assignment is applied BEFORE the actor acts for the six *-stale rows; prepareAudience must report staleEffective before the declaration; the actor receives its own declaration live (accepted) and in the replay after the restart; the watcher holds only the public lock.

A3 (same-side visibility, MISSION-MATCH-1): there is no teammate row; the opposing-actor negative is kept and renamed (opposing actor, not second actor). Same-side teammate visibility is MISSION-MATCH-1's Jest rows and A2's coop-restart row.

A4 (fixture position): staleEffective is the first-position witness of the A2F fixture, not a claim about product ownership after MISSION-MATCH-1 (owner is sideOfPlayer). The spectator guard precedes ownership in MatchWireSealedChoices, so the stale rows stay discriminating.

A5 (GM disclosure): the real mission GM keeps the player viewer role (known issue, Root ruling option a); GM rows are policy coverage only; A2M never infers GM from hostPlayerId, coop-gm or campaign UI labels.
A6 (pre-reveal authority): the six GM spectator rows record the pre-reveal authority sequences (authorityBeforeReveal) instead of asserting their absence (OQ-M1).
A7 (unrun obligations): every built-image behaviour, including R6-R8 and P1/P4/P6, is owed at RED/GREEN on the exact-main image; nothing in this admission is a built-image PASS.
